items.title: 15 Years of Duct Tape: Why IaC Adoption Stalled at 30%
items.summary: Struggling to scale Infrastructure as Code? This post explains why CI/CD pipelines and Git workflows break down for modern cloud infrastructure, how brittle IaC practices slow teams, and why a new foundation—pipeline-less delivery with built-in policy, compliance, and orchestration—can help DevOps scale and empower developers safely.

items.title: Drift Is Preventable
items.summary: It’s a Symptom of Platform Design, Not Developer Behavior.

items.title: Little Orphan Kube-Proxy
items.summary: AWS forces users to handle the management of kube-proxy in EKS clusters. If you're experiencing strange network behavior in a long-lived EKS cluster, this could be the problem. Let's go over some solutions.

items.title: The Case for Abstractions in IaC
items.summary: Most Infrastructure as Code implementations expose too much complexity, forcing developers to make infrastructure decisions they shouldn’t have to. This post explores why generic IaC modules fail, how to design abstractions that encode organizational standards while intentionally omitting irrelevant configurations, and how to shift ops from gatekeeping to enablement.

items.title: GitOps is not the right tool for the job
items.summary: GitOps isn’t the right fit for modern Ops, DevOps, or platform engineering. Learn why static workflows fail to address dynamic cloud complexity and explore better tools for managing real-time infrastructure.

items.title: The Missing Revolution in Operations: Scaling Expertise in a Cloud-First World
items.summary: Operations engineering is stuck in the past. This post breaks down why ops hasn’t had the same revolution as software development, explores the limits of DevOps, and argues for scaling expertise through reusable tools and clean abstractions. It’s time for ops to adopt lessons from software engineering and move the industry forward.

items.title: Convention over Configuration: Building Developer-Friendly IaC with OpenTofu
items.summary: Learn how to implement convention-over-configuration for Infrastructure as Code (IaC) using OpenTofu. Discover practical techniques to build developer-friendly IaC modules that streamline compliance, enforce business standards, and reduce operational friction.

items.title: OpenTofu Foundations: Tooling and Best Practices (Part 10)
items.summary: Welcome to Week 10 of our OpenTofu Foundations series! This week, we’ll focus on essential tools that ensure your OpenTofu configurations are reliable, secure, and maintainable. By the end of this session, you’ll have enabled key tools, understood their value, and integrated them into your workflow.

items.title: OpenTofu Foundations: Advanced State Management with OpenTofu (Part 9)
items.summary: In this webinar, we'll look at advanced strategies for using and manipulating the statefile. If you work with OpenTofu (or Terraform) long enough, you **will** have to repair, modify, or recover state. Guaranteed.

items.title: OpenTofu Foundations: Understanding State Management (Part 8)
items.summary: Welcome to Week 8 of our OpenTofu Foundations series! In this session, we'll delve into how OpenTofu manages the state of your infrastructure. Understanding state is crucial for effectively using OpenTofu, especially when working with teams and multiple environments. We’ll explore state files, secure storage options, and state locking strategies to ensure your infrastructure remains consistent and secure.

items.title: OpenTofu Foundations: Multi-Environment Management with OpenTofu (Part 7)
items.summary: In this session we will learn how to manage multiple deployments with the same OpenTofu configuration. We will learn about workspaces which are OpenTofu's built in mechanism for managing multiple state backends. Next we will cover some tricks to make managing workspaces less error prone for users. Lastly we will look at Checkov and how to implement security and policy scanning to ensure your deployments meet your compliance needs.

items.title: Convention over Configuration: Building Developer-Friendly IaC with OpenTofu
items.summary: Learn how to implement Convention over Configuration principles in your Infrastructure as Code using OpenTofu, making your IaC more maintainable and developer-friendly.

items.title: OpenTofu Foundations: Testing and Validation with OpenTofu (Part 6)
items.summary: Learn how to incorporate testing and validation into your OpenTofu workflows. This session will focus on tools and practices for testing your infrastructure code, including syntax validation, resource policy checks, and simulating infrastructure changes before applying them.

items.title: Getting Started with OpenTofu on Azure
items.summary: OpenTofu is an infrastructure-as-code tool that lets you define both cloud and on-prem resources in human-readable configuration files that you can version, reuse, and share. This post will help you get started using OpenTofu to manage your Azure resources.

items.title: OpenTofu Foundations: Integrating OpenTofu into CI/CD Pipelines (Part 5)
items.summary: Integrate OpenTofu into CI/CD pipelines to automate infrastructure deployments. Set up a pipeline to test, validate, and apply configurations reliably.

items.title: OpenTofu Foundations: Advanced Resource Management (Part 4)
items.summary: Welcome to week four of the OpenTofu Foundations workshop! This week, we'll dive into some of the advanced strategies for managing OpenTofu resources, including data sources, loops, conditionals, dynamic blocks, and lifecycle rules.

items.title: OpenTofu Foundations: Functions and Control Structures (Part 3)
items.summary: Welcome to week three of the OpenTofu workshop This week, we'll dive into functions and control structures. 90% of what we do as programmers is validate unknown data being passed to our programs, and manipulating imperfect data so we can connect software modules together. Functions help us provide a better more intuitive user experience and keep our code clean.

items.title: Are We Approaching Infrastructure as Code the Wrong Way?
items.summary: As platform engineers, DevOps professionals, and operations experts, our primary role is to empower developers—to make them more efficient, to help them ship faster and more confidently.

items.title: OpenTofu Foundations: Building Composable Infrastructure-as-Code Modules (Part 2)
items.summary: Welcome to week two of the OpenTofu workshop! This week, we'll dive into the concept of modular infrastructure using OpenTofu. Modules are a powerful way to organize your code, promote reusability, and enforce best practices in Infrastructure as Code (IaC). By the end of this session, you'll be able to create your own modules, use existing ones, and apply best practices for modular infrastructure design.

items.title: OpenTofu Foundations: Getting Started with OpenTofu (Part 1)
items.summary: Welcome to week one of the OpenTofu workshop! In this module, you'll learn how to create an EC2 instance running Wordpress, set up a MariaDB database, and configure basic infrastructure in AWS. We’ll go through creating instances, security groups, and databases while discussing key Terraform/OpenTofu concepts.

items.title: OpenTofu Foundations - A FREE Weekly Workshop to Build your IaC Skills
items.summary: Are you ready to dive into the world of Infrastructure as Code (IaC) with OpenTofu? We're excited to introduce this 10-week series, designed to take you from a beginner to a confident practitioner of OpenTofu. Whether you're just starting out with IaC or looking to solidify your knowledge of OpenTofu, this workshop is for you.
